tier1.text: Each globus pallidus helps control movement and lies deep inside the brain. It belongs to the basal nuclei, linked groups of brain cells involved in movement and motivation. It sits next to the putamen, another basal nucleus, and they fit together like curved lenses. It has two parts, an outer segment and an inner segment.

quotes.quote: The major structures of the basal nuclei that control movement are the caudate, putamen, and globus pallidus, which are located deep in the cerebrum.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The globus pallidus is a layered nucleus that lies just medial to the putamen; they are called the lenticular nuclei because they look like curved pieces fitting together like lenses.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: putamen: nucleus deep in the cerebrum that is part of the basal nuclei; along with the caudate, it is part of the striatum

quotes.quote: The globus pallidus has two subdivisions, the external and internal segments, which are lateral and medial, respectively.
